# Presentation outline (12 slides, about 12 minutes)

*Generated by `src/evaluation/make_report_assets.py`; every number comes from `results/metrics/`. Speaker notes are short on purpose.*

**1. Title and framing.** Heart Disease Risk Modelling via Bayesian Networks and Feed-Forward Neural Networks. Academic ML comparison, **not** a diagnostic system. Team names to be added.

**2. Problem statement.** Predict angiographic heart disease (binary) from 13 clinical and test variables. Question: do a domain-informed Bayesian network, Naive Bayes and a small MLP differ in *ranking* and in *probability calibration*, and how uncertain is the answer on 303 patients?

**3. Motivation and literature.** Calibrated probabilities matter for decision support (Steyerberg 2010; Van Calster 2019). BN theory (Pearl 1988; Koller & Friedman 2009); Naive Bayes can rank well despite violated independence (Domingos & Pazzani 1997); neural networks are not consistently better on tabular data (Shwartz-Ziv & Armon 2022; Grinsztajn et al. 2022); nested CV and leakage (Varma & Simon 2006; Cawley & Talbot 2010; Kapoor & Narayanan 2023). No systematic survey of studies on this dataset was done.

**4. Dataset and EDA.** UCI Cleveland (Detrano et al. 1989; CC BY 4.0). 303 rows, 14 columns, no duplicates. Missing: ca 4, thal 2. `num` counts 0-4: 164/55/36/35/13. Binary target: 164 negative, 139 positive (45.9%): mild imbalance. Figures: target distribution, correlation heatmap. Caveats: one centre, referral bias, predictors come from specialist tests.

**5. Feature engineering and leakage control.** Feature types: continuous / binary / ordinal / nominal. MLP: impute, standardise, one-hot (20 inputs). BN and NB: train-fold tertile bins, integer codes (13 inputs). Everything is fitted on the training fold only and refitted in every inner and outer fold; a guard rejects the target as a predictor.

**6. Bayesian network.** 14 nodes, 16 edges, fixed before evaluation (risk factors -> disease -> manifestations). Only the probability tables are learned (Dirichlet smoothing). Edges are assumptions (domain / modelling / weak), **not** causal claims. Figure: `bn_structure.png`.

**7. Naive Bayes.** Class -> every predictor; assumes conditional independence given the class (violated: oldpeak/slope, cp/exang, thalach/age). Same inputs and smoothing as the BN, so the comparison isolates structure.

**8. MLP.** 20 -> 16 -> 8 -> 1, ReLU, dropout, 481 parameters. BCE loss, Adam, weight decay, early stopping on a hold-out of the training fold. Hidden sizes and stopping rule fixed in advance; weight decay and dropout tuned in the inner loop.

**9. Experimental design.** 25 identical outer folds (5x5 stratified, seed 42); nested 5-fold inner CV on log loss; fixed 0.5 threshold, secondary Youden threshold from training data only; 2000-sample paired patient bootstrap. Integrity checks and a leakage test (shuffled outer labels change no prediction).

**10. Results.** Fold-level ROC AUC: BN 0.912, NB 0.907, MLP 0.907. Pooled ROC AUC with 95% CI: BN 0.909 [0.873, 0.939], NB 0.904 [0.869, 0.935], MLP 0.903 [0.868, 0.936]. Paired AUC differences all include 0: no evidence of a ranking difference. Sensitivity 0.787-0.803, specificity 0.848-0.865 at 0.5. Figures: ROC, PR, confusion matrices.

**11. Calibration and interpretation.** Brier: BN 0.127, NB 0.134, MLP 0.121. Calibration slope: BN 0.62, NB 0.51, MLP 1.10 (below 1 = over-confident). Log-loss differences exclude zero for NB-MLP and BN-NB; Brier and AUC differences do not; exploratory, no multiplicity correction. SHAP and permutation importance for the MLP agree on ca, cp, thal, then oldpeak; they describe the model, not causes.

**12. Limitations, conclusion and future work.** Limits: 303 patients, one centre, internal validation only, mode imputation, truncated BN/NB smoothing grid (top value chosen in 25/25 and 25/25 folds), assumed BN structure. Conclusion: equal ranking, MLP better calibrated; no superiority or clinical claim. Future: wider pre-declared grids and recalibration, structure learning, multiple imputation, external validation, subgroup analysis. Live demo (about 2 minutes): `streamlit run app/streamlit_app.py` - Model results page, then the Risk estimator with the disclaimer visible.
